ca_lower_basin.blurb: Lower Basin is a small cluster of eight boulder problems within Boulder Basin on Black Mountain, in the San Jacinto Mountains. The blocks stand next to the road just before the main campground begins, so there is almost no walking. The grade spread is wide: three problems at V1 or easier, two of them crack lines, then a steep jump to a handful running from V6 up to V10. Boulder Basin as a whole is a busy, campground-based zone with a lot of visitors, so a visit here pairs well with its other sectors.

ca_cal_trans_wall.blurb: Cal Trans Wall is a low-angle slab on the South Shore of Lake Tahoe, in the Meyers Area. It holds eight bolted sport routes between 5.6 and 5.9, which makes it a gentle place for newer leaders. Every line is close to a full 30 m, so a 60 m rope reaches the ground when lowering, and around ten quickdraws cover anything on the wall. The base sits just above a bike trail, so the walk is brief. The same area also has harder slab at Guntower Wall and a few multipitch lines nearby.
ca_cal_trans_wall.approach: Follow the mountain bike trail from the rusted green gate. The unmarked climbers' trail splits off and heads straight up the hill; push between bushes to reach the right end of the wall.

ca_eyes_boulder.blurb: Eyes Boulder is one of eight boulders that make up The Otherworld, a far corner of Druid Stones in the Bishop area of the Eastern Sierra. It has eight problems and almost all of them are gentle: four at VB, three at V0 and one at V1, plus a lip traverse, which suits beginners or a warm-up. The rock is good, with a patina-featured wall that is easy to identify. A couple of loose-looking sections are obvious and simple to avoid. Nearby, the Hall of the Mountain Queens slab is the bigger draw of the sector.

ca_clyde_minaret.blurb: Clyde Minaret is a needle-shaped peak of about 12,280 ft in the Ritter and Minarets section of the High Sierra. It has eight alpine lines: three graded by class and five on the YDS scale, topping out around 5.9. The best-known line is a long, many-pitch route up the dark triangular southeast face. Even the easiest ways to the summit involve fourth-class climbing. Expect a long approach from the Reds Meadow side, with a base camp at Cecile Lake on the bench above Minaret Lake.

ca_fat_freddie_s_cat.blurb: Fat Freddie's Cat is a sizeable formation in Wonderland Valley, Joshua Tree National Park, tucked behind Freak Brothers Dome and facing east. It has eight routes, mostly trad, with a single sport line and one top rope. Grades stretch from 5.2 to 5.11, and 5.9 is the most common number. The walk in goes beyond the dome and up a broad valley, then finishes with a short scramble to the main block. A gully at the top gives a walk-off from the best-known two-pitch line.
